s: Herodotos of Thebes has new country Orchomenos
q: and his new country Orchomenos, which, when he drave ashore on a wrecked ship, harboured him amid his dismal hap

s: Herodotos of Thebes seeks wreaths from Pytho and choice wreaths from Alpheos (yet again)
q: Now may Herodotos, up-borne upon the sweet-voiced Muse's shining wings, yet again with wreaths from Pytho and choice wreaths from Alpheos from the Olympian games entwine his hand, and bring honour unto seven-gated Thebes.

s: Asopodoros is banished from Thebes (seems to have been)
q: Asopodoros seems to have been banished from Thebes and kindly received in his banishment by Orchomenos.

s: Orchomenos receives Asopodoros (kindly, in his banishment)
q: Asopodoros seems to have been banished from Thebes and kindly received in his banishment by Orchomenos.

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is a winner (in the chariot-race)
q: FOR XENOKRATES OF AKRAGAS, WINNER IN THE CHARIOT-RACE.

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is august citizens (in converse)
q: In converse with citizens was he august

s: Xenokrates of Akragas upholds horse-racing (after the Hellenes' wont)
q: and upheld horse-racing after the Hellenes' wont

s: Xenokrates of Akragas worships gods (at all festivals)
q: also worshipped he at all festivals of the gods

s: Xenokrates of Akragas practices hospitality (on an extensive scale)
q: nor ever did the breeze that breathed around his hospitable board give him cause to draw in his sail, but with the summer-gales he would fare unto Phasis, and in his winter voyage unto the shores of Nile

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is the father of Thrasyboulos
q: Let not Thrasyboulos now, because that jealous hopes beset the mind of mortals, be silent concerning his father's prowess

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is the brother of Theron
q: both Xenokrates and his brother Theron seem to be spoken of in this ode as already dead

s: Thrasyboulos is associated with hospitality (his house is known for it)
q: For no stranger is your house, O Thrasyboulos, to pleasant shouts of triumph, neither to sweet-voiced songs.

s: Theron is a son (of Ainesidamos)
q: where the sons[4] of Ainesidamos attained unto honour everlasting

s: Xenokrates of Akragas wins chariot-race (at the Isthmian Games)
q: I sing, while I do honour to the Isthmian victory won by speed of horses, which to Xenokrates did Poseidon give

s: Theron is the brother of Xenokrates of Akragas
q: both Xenokrates and his brother Theron seem to be spoken of in this ode as already dead

s: Akragas is the home of Xenokrates of Akragas (he is a light of its people)
q: a man of goodly chariot, a light of the people of Akragas.

s: Isthmian Games is won by speed of horses (at the Isthmian Games)
q: I sing, while I do honour to the Isthmian victory won by speed of horses

s: Olympic games are proclaimed by Elean truce-bringers (with an accompanying universal truce)
q: The heralds who proclaimed throughout Hellas the approach of the Olympic games, and an universal solemn truce during their celebration.

s: Elean truce-bringers are heralds of Zeus (the son of Kronos)
q: the heralds of the seasons[3], the Elean truce-bringers of Zeus the son of Kronos

s: Zeus is the son of Kronos
q: the Elean truce-bringers of Zeus the son of Kronos

s: Ainesidamos is the father of Theron (one of his sons honored at Olympia)
q: where the sons[4] of Ainesidamos attained unto honour everlasting

s: Xenokrates of Akragas receives Dorian parsley wreath (for his Isthmian victory)
q: which to Xenokrates did Poseidon give, and sent to him a wreath of Dorian parsley to bind about his hair

s: Muse is associated with lyre (in the Muse's car)
q: The men of old, Thrasyboulos, who went up into the Muse's car to give welcome with the loud-voiced lyre

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is associated with Poseidon (as the god who granted his victory)
q: which to Xenokrates did Poseidon give, and sent to him a wreath of Dorian parsley to bind about his hair

s: Xenokrates of Akragas has chariot (a goodly chariot)
q: a man of goodly chariot, a light of the people of Akragas.

s: Xenokrates of Akragas receives glory from Apollo (at Krisa)
q: Also at Krisa did far-prevailing Apollo look upon him, and gave him there too glory

s: Xenokrates of Akragas wins Erectheidai (crowns at Athens)
q: and again when he attained unto the crowns of the Erectheidai in shining Athens

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is honored at Olympic games (through the victory of the sons of Ainesidamos)
q: they gave him greeting for that he had fallen at the knees of golden Victory in their land which men call the holy place of Olympic Zeus, where the sons[4] of Ainesidamos attained unto honour everlasting

s: Xenokrates of Akragas is a light (of the people of Akragas)
q: a man of goodly chariot, a light of the people of Akragas.

s: Isthmian Ode III is for Melissos of Thebes (winner in the pankration)
q: FOR MELISSOS OF THEBES, WINNER IN THE PANKRATION.

s: Melissos of Thebes receives training from Orseas (his trainer)
q: after another won already among the boys, for that he had regard unto the many counsels of him who was the pilot of his helm[5]. And with Orseas' name I join him in my triumphal song

s: Kleonymid clan flourishes continually (in favour with God)
q: wherein the Kleonymidai flourish continually, and in favour with God pass onward through the term of mortal life

s: Kleonymid clan is honored at Thebes (from the beginning)
q: These men verily are spoken of as having honour at Thebes from the beginning

s: Kleonymid clan is related to Labdakidai (through the maternal line)
q: also on the mother's side being akin to the Labdakidai his race hath been conversant with riches

s: Kleonymid clan has chariot tradition chariot (wealth spent on horses and racing)
q: For neither did they refrain to contend with the curved chariot in the great meetings of the people, but they had delight to strive with the whole folk of Hellas in spending their wealth on steeds.

s: Kleonymid clan loses members in battle of the Kleonymid clan (four men killed in one day)
q: but in one day the fierce snow-storm of war hath made a happy hearth to be desolate of four men.

s: Kleonymid clan regains glory (after a period of decline)
q: But now once more after that wintry gloom hath it blossomed, even as in the flowery months the earth blossometh with red roses, according to the counsels of gods.

s: Zeus bestows Mortal excellence (on mortals)
q: But from thee, O Zeus, cometh all high excellence to mortals

s: Zeus sustains fortune (for those who honor him)
q: longer liveth their bliss who have thee in honour

s: Isthmian Ode III honors Melissos of Thebes (as pankration victor)
q: May we find favour with the Muses, that for Melissos too we kindle such beacon-blaze of song, a worthy prize of the pankration for this scion of Telesias' son.

s: Poseidon is associated with Isthmos (as its inhabitant and divine patron)
q: For the Shaker of Earth who inhabiteth Onchestos and the Bridge[2] between seas that lieth before the valley of Corinth

s: Poseidon restores glory (to the Kleonymid house through the hymn)
q: now giveth to the house this hymn of wonder, and leadeth up out of her bed the ancient glory of the famous deeds thereof

s: Herakles's wrestling match with Antaios is compared to pankration (Melissos's contest against his opponents)
q: The ode compares his match against his antagonists with that of Herakles against the African giant Antaios.

s: Herakles is a son of Alkmene (divine hero)
q: even the son of Alkmene, he who ascended up to Olympus

s: Herakles dwells in Olympus (among the immortals)
q: And now beside the aegis-bearer he dwelleth, possessing happiness most fair

s: Herakles is married to Hebe (in Olympus)
q: and hath Hebe to wife

s: Herakles is honored by immortals (as their friend)
q: and hath honour from the immortals as their friend

s: Antaios is a giant (African)
q: with that of Herakles against the African giant Antaios.

s: Antaios has temple roofed with skulls (skulls of strangers)
q: that he might cause him to cease from roofing Poseidon's temple with the skulls of strangers

s: Herakles has Herakles's altar-ring (at Elektrai)
q: Unto his honour upon the heights Elektrai we of this city prepare a feast and new-built altar-ring

s: Aias commits Aias's suicide (beneath the far-spent night)
q: Verily ye know the bloody deed of Aias, that he wrought beneath the far-spent night, when he smote himself through with his own sword

s: Homer honors Aias (through poetic song)
q: But lo! Homer hath done him honour among men

s: Homeric song delivers glory (to bards after him to sing)
q: by raising up his excellence in the fulness thereof hath through the rod[3] of his divine lays delivered it to bards after him to sing

s: Muses are invoked for beacon-blaze of song (for Melissos)
q: May we find favour with the Muses, that for Melissos too we kindle such beacon-blaze of song

s: Melissos of Thebes belongs to Thebes (his home)
q: in the hollow vale of the deep-chested lion being winner in the chariot-race he made proclamation that his home was Thebes.

s: Melissos of Thebes provides an ample means (in the Isthmian games)
q: for thou hast shown forth to me, O Melissos, in the Isthmian games an ample means to follow in song the excellence of thy race

s: Melissos of Thebes wins Nemean chariot victory (in the chariot-race)
q: Of two prizes is the lot fallen to Melissos, to turn his heart unto sweet mirth, for in the glens of Isthmos hath he won crowns, and again in the hollow vale of the deep-chested lion being winner in the chariot-race he made proclamation that his home was Thebes.

s: Melissos of Thebes has stature small (despite which he prevailed)
q: For not of the stature of Orion was this man, but his presence is contemptible, yet terrible is he to grapple with in his strength.

s: Melissos of Thebes has courage lion-like (in the struggle)
q: He being like unto the roaring lions in courage taketh unto him their spirit to be his own in the struggle

s: Melissos of Thebes has cunning fox-like (in combat)
q: but in sleight he is as the fox that spreadeth out her feet[4] and preventeth the swoop of the eagle

s: Isthmian Ode IV is for Phylakidas of Aigina (winner in the pankration)
q: FOR PHYLAKIDAS OF AIGINA, WINNER IN THE PANKRATION.

s: Pytheas is brother of Phylakidas of Aigina
q: This Phylakidas was a son of Lampon, and a brother of the Pytheas for whom the fifth Nemean was written.

s: Pytheas wins a pankratiast's crown (at Nemea)
q: For thee, Phylakidas, a double glory of valour is at Isthmos stored, and at Nemea both for thee and for Pytheas a pankratiast's crown.

s: Pytheas has crown at Nemean Games (as a pankratiast)
q: For thee, Phylakidas, a double glory of valour is at Isthmos stored, and at Nemea both for thee and for Pytheas a pankratiast's crown.

s: Theia is mother of Sun
q: Mother of the Sun, Theia of many names

s: Theia is mother of Moon (according to Hesiod)
q: She, according to Hesiod, was the mother of the Sun, the Moon, and the Morning

s: Theia is mother of Morning (according to Hesiod)
q: She, according to Hesiod, was the mother of the Sun, the Moon, and the Morning

s: Theia has name Euruphaessa
q: and was also called [Greek: Euruphaessa] and [Greek: chruse]

s: Theia has name chruse
q: and was also called [Greek: Euruphaessa] and [Greek: chruse]

s: wealth supports life's bloom (when joined with good success and fair fame)
q: Two things alone there are that cherish life's bloom to its utmost sweetness amidst the fair flowers of wealth--to have good success and to win therefore fair fame.

s: Isthmian Ode IV celebrates Phylakidas of Aigina (as pankration winner)
q: FOR PHYLAKIDAS OF AIGINA, WINNER IN THE PANKRATION.

s: games grant glory (through victory and wreaths)
q: And that man also hath won longed-for glory in the strife of games, for whose strong hand or fleet foot abundant wreaths have bound his hair.

s: pankration involves the struggle of hands that bring limbs low
q: Also have I praise for Pytheas, for that he guided aright[4] the course of Phylakidas' blows in the struggle of hands that bring limbs low, an adversary he of cunning soul.

s: Zeus orders events (as lord of all)
q: Yet let no boast be heard. Zeus ordereth this or that, Zeus, lord of all.

s: Aigina is home of Aiakids (the island's heroic lineage)
q: But in Oinone the great souls of Aiakos and his sons

s: Aigina is a island (glorious and a tower of high-adventuring valour)
q: Even they whose home my mouth proclaimeth to be Aigina's glorious isle: a tower is she, builded from long ago, to tempt the climb of high-adventuring valour.

s: Aigina has equal laws commonwealth
q: in company of the Graces am I come for sake of Lampon's sons to this commonwealth of equal laws[1].

s: Aigina helps deliver Salamis (through its seamen in the battle of Salamis)
q: but now in war might Aias' city, Salamis, bear witness thereto in her deliverance by Aigina's seamen amid the destroying tempest of Zeus

s: Salamis is a city (Aias' city)
q: might Aias' city, Salamis, bear witness thereto

s: battle of Salamis involves Aigina (Aiginian seamen help deliver Salamis)
q: Salamis, bear witness thereto in her deliverance by Aigina's seamen amid the destroying tempest of Zeus, when death came thick as hail on the unnumbered hosts.

s: Isthmian Ode IV dates to shortly after the battle of Salamis (probably B.C. 478)
q: This ode must have been written shortly after the battle of Salamis, probably B.C. 478, and was to be sung at Aigina, perhaps at a festival of the goddess Theia who is invoked at the beginning.

s: song preserves glory (of great warriors through immeasurable time)
q: For even the great men of old that were good warriors have profited of the telling of their tale, and are glorified on the lute and in the pipe's strains manifold, through immeasurable time

s: victory is honoured by song (in games)
q: Now in pleasant song even these honours also of the games welcome the joy for a fair victory.

s: Phylakidas of Aigina is a pankration winner
q: FOR PHYLAKIDAS OF AIGINA, WINNER IN THE PANKRATION.

s: Phylakidas of Aigina is son of Lampon
q: This Phylakidas was a son of Lampon, and a brother of the Pytheas for whom the fifth Nemean was written.

s: Phylakidas of Aigina is brother of Pytheas
q: This Phylakidas was a son of Lampon, and a brother of the Pytheas for whom the fifth Nemean was written.

s: Phylakidas of Aigina is son of Lampon
q: This Phylakidas was a son of Lampon, and a brother of the Pytheas for whom the fifth Nemean was written.

s: Phylakidas of Aigina has glory at Isthmian Games (for pankration)
q: For thee, Phylakidas, a double glory of valour is at Isthmos stored, and at Nemea both for thee and for Pytheas a pankratiast's crown.

s: Phylakidas of Aigina has crown at Nemean Games (as a pankratiast)
q: For thee, Phylakidas, a double glory of valour is at Isthmos stored, and at Nemea both for thee and for Pytheas a pankratiast's crown.

s: Phylakidas of Aigina is winner in the games (youngest son)
q: for that Phylakidas the youngest son is winner in the games.

s: Lampon is loved for kind entreating of strangers
q: and for his kind entreating of strangers is he loved

s: Lampon aspires to the just mean
q: to the just mean aspiring, to the just mean holding fast

s: Lampon has tongue aligned with thoughts (his speech matches his thoughts)
q: and his tongue departeth not from his thoughts

s: Aigina is a city (beloved by the gods)
q: and dwell here in a city which the gods love well.

s: Nemean Games is won by Psalychidai (by the family of Phylakidas, Pytheas, and Euthymenes)
q: Three victories have they won in the pankration of Isthmos, and others at leafy Nemea, even these noble sons and their mother's brother

s: Zeus is a god (Olympian deity and Saviour)
q: And be it ours to make ready yet a third for the Saviour[3], the Olympian one

s: Phylakidas of Aigina wins pankration (at the Isthmian Games)
q: for that Phylakidas the youngest son is winner in the games.

s: Zeus receives libation (the first bowl of song at Nemea)
q: Our first, O Zeus, was unto thee, when at Nemea we[1] won thy excellent crown

s: Zeus is addressed as father
q: If ever, O father Zeus, thou hast heard my prayer with willing heart

s: Poseidon rules Isthmos (called the lord of Isthmos)
q: and now is this second unto the lord[2] of Isthmos

s: Fates are called on Lampon
q: Now I call on high-throned Klotho and her sister Fates to draw nigh unto the praying of the man I love.

s: Aiakos' descendants are a golden-charioted seed (a heroic lineage)
q: And upon you also, golden-charioted seed of Aiakos

s: Aiakos' descendants have fame (spread beyond Egypt and among the Hyperboreans)
q: For innumerable hundred-foot[6] straight roads are cleft for your fair deeds to go forth, beyond the springs of Nile, and through the Hyperboreans' midst

s: Peleus is a son-in-law of gods (blissful)
q: that it knoweth not the fame of Peleus, that blissful son-in-law of gods

s: Phylakidas of Aigina is a winner (in the Isthmian Games)
q: FOR PHYLAKIDAS OF AIGINA, WINNER IN THE PANKRATION.

s: Telamon is a chief (leader of the company)
q: then did Telamon their chief challenge Amphitryon's son

s: Telamon is father of Aias
q: or of Aias son of Telamon

s: Aias is a son of Telamon (heroic warrior)
q: or of Aias son of Telamon

s: Aias is named after eagle (the bird that appeared to Herakles and Telamon)
q: also after the bird's name that had appeared unto them he said that the child's name should be the mighty Aias

s: Aias is a warrior (terrible in the strife of warring hosts)
q: the mighty Aias[8], terrible in the strife of warring hosts

s: Herakles is a son of Alkmene
q: Alkmene's son took with him in his ships to Troy

s: Herakles leads Tirynthian men (as an eager ally in war)
q: whom unto brazen war an eager ally with Tirynthian men Alkmene's son took with him in his ships to Troy

s: Herakles destroys Pergamos (captures the city)
q: There did Herakles take the city of Pergamos

s: Herakles kills Alkyoneus (at Phlegrai; a gigantic herdsman)
q: and the herdsman whose stature was as a mountain, Alkyoneus whom he found at Phlegrai

s: Phylakidas of Aigina is a son (youngest son of Lampon)
q: for that Phylakidas the youngest son is winner in the games.

s: Graces waters their clan of the Psalychidai (with the Charites' delicious dew)
q: they water with the Charites' delicious dew their clan of the Psalychidai

s: Muses provide song of triumph (for Phylakidas and his family)
q: for Phylakidas am I come, O Muse, a dispenser of thy triumphal songs

s: song of triumph is a song (dispensed by the Muses in celebration of victory)
q: for Phylakidas am I come, O Muse, a dispenser of thy triumphal songs

s: Mnemosyne is mother of Muses (the Muses are her daughters)
q: golden-robed Mnemosyne's deep-girdled daughters made once to spring out of the earth

s: Lampon is a son of Kleonikos
q: With such desires prayeth the son[4] of Kleonikos that he may fulfil them ere he meet death or hoary eld.

s: Lampon has athlete progeny (sons who compete successfully)
q: in honour of Lampon's athlete progeny.

s: Lampon practices all he doth (with discipline)
q: And Lampon, in that he bestoweth practice on all he doth, holdeth in high honour the word of Hesiod which speaketh thereof

s: Lampon exhorts his sons (to practice)
q: and exhorteth thereunto his sons

s: Thebes is a divine city
q: Wherewithal of the fair deeds done in thy land, O divine Thebe, hath thy soul had most delight?

s: Thebes sends home Adrastos (after strong battle; to Argos)
q: or when out of the noise of the strong battle-cry thou sentest Adrastos home to horse-breeding Argos, of his countless company forlorn?

s: Adrastos returns to horse-breeding Argos
q: thou sentest Adrastos home to horse-breeding Argos

s: Argos is a horse-breeding land
q: thou sentest Adrastos home to horse-breeding Argos

s: Thebes establishes Dorian colony of the men of Lakedaimon (according to the mythic tradition of the Herakleidai)
q: or when thou madest the Dorian colony of the men of Lakedaimon stand upright upon its feet

s: sons of Aigeus are descended from Thebes (as progeny)
q: and the sons of Aigeus thy progeny took Amyklai

s: Strepsiades of Thebes is a pankratiast
q: New triumph now lead for Strepsiades with melodious hymn: for at Isthmos hath he borne away the pankratiast's prize.

s: Strepsiades of Thebes wins pankration (at Isthmos)
q: for at Isthmos hath he borne away the pankratiast's prize

s: Thebes gives birth to Dionysos (in myth)
q: Whether when thou broughtest forth to the light Dionysos of the flowing hair, who sitteth beside Demeter to whom the cymbals clang?

s: Strepsiades of Thebes possesses wondrous strength
q: Wondrous in strength is he, and to look upon of goodly shape, and his valour is such as shameth not his stature.

s: Strepsiades of Thebes possesses goodly shape
q: Wondrous in strength is he, and to look upon of goodly shape, and his valour is such as shameth not his stature.

s: Strepsiades of Thebes possesses valour (proportionate to his stature)
q: his valour is such as shameth not his stature

s: Strepsiades of Thebes shares crown with Strepsiades's uncle (through the grace of the Muses)
q: So shineth he forth by grace of the Muses iris-haired, and to his uncle of like name hath he given to share his crown

s: Strepsiades's uncle is a warrior
q: for albeit bronze-shielded Ares gave him over unto death, yet remaineth there for the valiant a recompense of renown.

s: Strepsiades's uncle is killed by Ares (in battle)
q: for albeit bronze-shielded Ares gave him over unto death

s: Strepsiades's uncle is a son of Diodotos
q: So didst thou, son[3] of Diodotos, following the praise of the warrior Meleagros, and of Hektor, and of Amphiaraos

s: Strepsiades's uncle is compared with Meleagros (in warrior's praise)
q: following the praise of the warrior Meleagros, and of Hektor, and of Amphiaraos

s: Strepsiades's uncle is compared with Hektor (in warrior's praise)
q: following the praise of the warrior Meleagros, and of Hektor, and of Amphiaraos

s: Thebes receives Zeus (in myth, at Amphitryon's doors)
q: or when at midnight in a snow of gold thou didst receive the mightiest of the gods, what time he stood at Amphitryon's doors and beguiled his wife, to the begetting of Herakles?

s: Strepsiades's uncle is compared with Amphiaraos (in warrior's praise)
q: following the praise of the warrior Meleagros, and of Hektor, and of Amphiaraos

s: war is a struggle of fighters (with the bravest relying on slender hopes)
q: amid the company of fighters in the front, where the bravest on slenderest hopes bare up the struggle of war

s: song and poetic fame is associated with the glory of the old time (through the sounding stream of song)
q: the glory of the old time sleepeth, and mortals are unmindful thereof, save such as married to the sounding stream of song attaineth unto the perfect meed that wisdom[2] giveth

s: Poseidon is a earth-grasper
q: but now hath the earth-grasper[4] granted unto me a calm after the storm

s: Poseidon grants calm (after the storm)
q: but now hath the earth-grasper[4] granted unto me a calm after the storm

s: Pegasos is a winged horse
q: Thus did winged Pegasos throw his lord Bellerophon

s: Pegasos throws Bellerophon (when Bellerophon sought to enter the heavenly habitations)
q: Thus did winged Pegasos throw his lord Bellerophon, when he would fain enter into the heavenly habitations and mix among the company of Zeus.

s: Bellerophon seeks to enter heavenly habitations (to mix among the company of Zeus)
q: when he would fain enter into the heavenly habitations and mix among the company of Zeus

s: Pythian Games award crown (to the speaker, as requested)
q: But to us, O Loxias of the golden-flowing hair, give also at thy Pythian games a new fair-flowering crown.

s: Zeus begets Herakles (with Amphitryon's wife, in myth)
q: what time he stood at Amphitryon's doors and beguiled his wife, to the begetting of Herakles?

s: Amphitryon's wife is beguiled by Zeus (in myth)
q: what time he stood at Amphitryon's doors and beguiled his wife, to the begetting of Herakles?

s: Thebes is honored in Teiresias (for wise counsels)
q: Or when thou hadst honour in the wise counsels of Teiresias

s: Thebes is associated with Iolaos (as a cunning charioteer)
q: or in Iolaos the cunning charioteer

s: Hellas is cursed by Tantalos-stone (as an intolerable curse)
q: inasmuch as some god hath put away from us the Tantalos-stone that hung above our heads, a curse intolerable to Hellas.

s: Freedom enables mortals (to cure the crookedness of life)
q: yet if Freedom abide with them, even such things may mortals cure.

s: Thebes is called seven-gated
q: whom seven-gated Thebes reared

s: Thebes rears Pindar (as his city)
q: whom seven-gated Thebes reared

s: Zeus is father of Aiakos (through Aigina)
q: and lay with thee, whence to the sire of great thunderings thou didst bear the godlike Aiakos, best of men upon the earth.

s: Aiakos is a decider of strife (even among divinities)
q: This man even among divinities became a decider of strife

s: Aiakos' descendants is descended from Aiakos (through his sons and grandsons)
q: his godlike sons and his sons' sons delighting in battle were foremost in valour when they met in the ringing brazen melley

s: Kleandros wins reward of victory (at Isthmos)
q: For Kleandros in his prime let some of you, ye young men, go stand before the shining portal of his father Telesarchos, and rouse a song of triumph, to be a glorious recompense of his toils, for that he hath achieved reward of victory at Isthmos, and hath showed his strength in the games of Nemea.

s: Aiakos' descendants is glorified by Achilles (through his heroic deeds)
q: Unto all these did Achilles, champion of the Aiakid race, point the way to the house of Persephone, and thereby did he glorify Aigina and the root whence he was sprung.

s: Poseidon desires Thetis (as a bride)
q: for the hand of Thetis there was strife between Zeus and glorious Poseidon, each having desire that she should be his fair bride

s: Themis prophesies oracle concerning Thetis' son (in the council of the immortals)
q: For Themis of wise counsels spake in the midst of them of how it was pre-destined that the sea-goddess should bear a royal offspring mightier than his father

s: oracle concerning Thetis' son foretells Thetis' son (that he will be mightier than his father)
